title: Get Your 401k Match In Three Steps

beats.say: Your boss may be offering you up to eighteen hundred dollars a year, and you might be turning it down.
beats.visual: a small unopened envelope lying on a dark wooden desk under a warm lamp, no text

beats.say: It is called the employer match. Here is how to claim yours in three steps.
beats.visual: three wooden doors in a row in a quiet hallway, the middle one slightly open with light

beats.say: Step one. Find your match. Ask human resources or open your plan page and look for the matching formula.
beats.visual: a hand sliding a thin folder across a polished desk, close-up, no face

beats.say: A common example is fifty cents for every dollar you put in, up to six percent of your pay.
beats.visual: a glass jar slowly filling with small gold coins, macro shot, soft light

beats.say: Step two. Contribute enough to get the full match, and no less.
beats.visual: a stack of coins and a matching smaller stack placed side by side, dramatic side light

beats.say: On a sixty thousand dollar pay, six percent is thirty six hundred a year, and the match adds about eighteen hundred.
beats.visual: a tall stack of gold coins growing beside a smaller stack on black marble

beats.say: Step three. Check your vesting schedule, so you know when the match is fully yours.
beats.visual: a single stone step leading up a long quiet staircase into morning mist, no people

beats.say: Some plans make you wait a few years before the match belongs to you, so know the date.
beats.visual: a small plant slowly growing in a sunny windowsill pot, time lapse feel, no people

beats.say: Here is the part nobody tells you. Skipping the match is like turning down part of your paycheck.
beats.visual: an open empty wallet beside a pair of scissors on a dark table, moody light

beats.say: The honest catch: not every employer offers a match, and the formula changes from plan to plan.
beats.visual: a heavy iron gate half open onto a foggy path, no people

beats.say: Check your own plan rules before you change anything.
beats.visual: an old paper map being unfolded on a wooden table, hands out of focus

beats.say: This is education, not advice. A few minutes this week could matter for years.
beats.visual: a quiet kitchen table at morning with a coffee cup and a notepad, no people

beats.say: Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: an empty highway stretching toward a glowing sunrise horizon, wide shot

caption: Step one: find your 401k match. Step two: contribute enough to get all of it. Step three: check the vesting schedule so you keep it. An example, not advice; plans vary. Educational content, not financial advice.
description: Your 401k match may be pay you are leaving unclaimed. Three steps to find it, claim it and keep it. An example, not advice; plans and vesting rules vary.
first_comment: Do you know your employer's match? Educational only, not financial advice.

facts.claim: Many employers offer a 401k match; formulas vary (for example 50 cents per dollar up to 6% of pay)
Matching contributions may be subject to a vesting schedule
